scope: independent root audit of the mixed-kernel endpoint identity, uniform and L1 cost bounds, global coefficient inequality, conditional Legendre threshold, degree-one replacement, and zero booking

checks.root_repairs: Corrected two TeX omissions, made B0>0 explicit in the inverse-cost hypothesis, and replaced the falsely strict all-tuple coefficient bound by the correct weak inequality; strictness is retained away from the zero tuple. Clarified the rational-endpoint form of Legendre's theorem.

mathematical_audit.endpoint: For S=x(x-1)R, P(0)=A+S(0)+S'(0)=A-R(0), hence F(0)=5A-R(0). An integer endpoint of uniform norm below one must vanish, giving R(0)=5A and P(0)=-4A.
mathematical_audit.L1_dichotomy: The derivative satisfies |F'|<=3(B0+B1+|A|)=Lambda. If the nonzero integer endpoint has magnitude at least one, integrating 1-Lambda*x on [0,1/Lambda] gives norm_1(F)>=1/(2Lambda).
mathematical_audit.coefficient_bound: The identity norm_1(4A/(1+x^2))=pi|A| and the triangle inequality give 3|A|<=norm_1(F)+2B0. Equality can occur only in the zero-tuple edge case at the weakened bound, so >= is the correct global statement.
mathematical_audit.continued_fraction: Under B0>0, explicit nonvanishing, and norm_1(F)<min(1,1/(2B0)), A is nonzero and the global bound gives B0>|A|. Dividing by |A| yields error below 1/(2|A|^2); reduction can only decrease the denominator, so Legendre applies without assuming the desired irrationality.
mathematical_audit.degree_one_replacement: The same endpoint pair has P_(A,C)=A+(A-C)x. From |A alpha-C|<1 and alpha<7, its coefficient norm is below 9|A|+1<=9B0+1.
mathematical_audit.scope_limit: The theorem proves a cost barrier and classification. It neither constructs a structured sequence nor proves its nonvanishing, so it supplies no irrationality conclusion.
